blocking_findings.summary: Wall-clock assertion (<=10 s for 200 recipes, i.e. 50 ms/line) is flaky on a loaded host and fails the control, and therefore rig-check-control inside make test.
blocking_findings.evidence: Idle-ish host: 5.1 s (make 3.81) and 5.6 s (gmake) for the 200-line fixture, already half the budget with load average 16 from a running rig/full. With 12 busy loops: failed 3/3 (52-61 s runs). With 6 busy loops: failed 3/3, then passed 2/2 minutes later. During mutation runs at load 5-9 on 16 cores it failed in about 15 of 25 independent runs (appearing as an extra failed case beside the intended one). A sibling cpu-busy-sleep case also flaked once at load 9.
blocking_findings.reproduce: pids=; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do (while :; do :; done) & pids="$pids $!"; done; for i in 1 2 3; do sh tools/test_suite_profile.sh overhead-200 | tail -2; done; for p in $pids; do kill $p; done
blocking_findings.why_blocking: The control runs inside make test on a rig that is routinely loaded (iteration 55 recorded a load-related failed rig run costing 117 min). A false red here blocks merges with no code fault.
blocking_findings.suggested_fix: Make the bound relative: time the same 200 lines under the same make with plain SHELL and assert overhead per line against that, or assert only on row count plus a very loose bound (e.g. 60 s), or retry once; keep the 50 ms/line figure as a report-only measurement.

non_blocking_findings: Report refusal rules unguarded by the control (mutants survive): failed-run rc refusal, jobs validation (before must be 1, after 6 or 8), closure mismatch inside report, duplicate-slot refusal (the fixture appends slot=b1 attempt=1 so it fails on the count, not on duplicate), and the -j8 requirement.
compare accepts an empty closure_sha256 on both sides (removing the -n check survives); only a differing hash is tested.
CPU accounting: dropping system CPU (user-only) survives; only busy-vs-sleep ratios are asserted.
Load sampler: not killing the in-flight sleep on cleanup survives (no orphan seen after 30 s, but untested); half-row guard for an empty load survives.

AC1 text expects 40 cases on both makes; on a host with only one distinct GNU make it reports 20 and prints the loud degrade line (verified with PATH hiding gmake: 20 cases rc0). With no GNU make at all it fails loudly rc1. Both are correct per the amendment.

Portability verified: the wrapper run under /bin/dash and the profiler under dash both pass 40/40 (times output format, awk minute parsing, load via sysctl then /proc/loadavg). Not verified on a real Linux box.
